candidate.statement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. You can return the answer in any order.
hints: For each element x, what value would complete the sum to target?
Can you store previously seen values and their indices in a hash map?
short_diagnostics: Why must the check `target - num in seen` precede inserting `seen[num] = i`?

evaluator.rubric: Learner checks for complement before inserting current value to prevent matching an element with itself.
known_pitfalls: Inserting into dictionary before checking, causing self-pairing when target == 2 * num.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Single-pass dictionary lookup operates in O(N) time and O(N) space.
